findings.title: Defense is never validated - any card id, including a nonexistent one, stops any attack, and the defense type is never matched to the attack type
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:298 "The card you are defending with must defend against the type of attack your opponent is performing." CRD:303-307 (correctly 304-308) enumerates the only five legal defenses (a starburst card from hand, a starburst Non-Combat in play, an MP effect, an effect from the Ally in control of Combat, or take the damage). CRD L793 "the card must be able to stop that same kind of attack"; glossary CRD L2525/L2549 define Energy Combat / Physical Combat cards as stopping their own kind of attack.
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:265-277 (resolveDefense); defenseStops at combat.ts:471-481; packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:150 forwards cardUid unvalidated
findings.defect: resolveDefense does `if (opts.cardUid && !opts.takeDamage) { atk.stopped = true; ... }`. It never looks the card up, never checks that the defender owns it, never checks that it carries a stopAttack/defense ability or a starburst, and never compares `atk.attackType`. The card id is used purely as a key for the optional combat-long lockout lookup, and defenseStops (combat.ts:471-481) searches every player's hand, inPlay and discard rather than the defender's hand. reducer.ts:150 does no validation either.
findings.consequence: Verified at runtime: `resolveDefense(state, { cardUid: 'totally-made-up-uid' }, { actingPlayerIdx: 1 }, db, [])` returned no error and logged "P1 stops the attack." Combined with rank 2 (nothing leaves hand), no attack ever has to land - a defender names any string and every attack in the game is stopped. Cross-type defense also works: Nappa's Energy Aura played against a PHYSICAL attack stops it and additionally locks the attacker out of all energy attacks for the rest of the combat. Defending is never a resource-matching decision.
findings.verifiedBy: combat.ts:265-266 is `if (opts.cardUid && !opts.takeDamage) {` / `    // Provisional: any offered defense card stops the attack (starburst check = coverage TODO).` followed by `atk.stopped = true;` - the comment is the engine admitting it. The uid is never resolved before the stop: the only lookup is defenseStops, and combat.ts:471-481 confirms it iterates `for (const p of state.players)` over `['hand', 'inPlay', 'discard']`, returns `[]` on a miss, and its result is only used for `if (e.window === 'thisCombat') addLockout(...)`. So a bogus uid falls through to `atk.stopped = true`. No ownership, starburst, or attack-type match anywhere - grep for `starburst` across packages and apps returns only two comments (combat.ts:266 and shared/abilities.ts:10), no code. No server-side validation either. CRD:298 and the five-option list at CRD:304-308 are quoted accurately (the range should be 304-308, not 303-307; line 303 is blank - immaterial). || Corroborated by the endurance-and-stops audit: the type is only consulted AFTER the stop, at combat.ts:269-271, purely to register the lockout; reducer.ts:150 is `err = resolveDefense(state, { ...(action.cardUid ? { cardUid: action.cardUid } : {}), ... })` with no validation, and grep of packages/server/src finds no defend validation. No test covers cross-type defense: lockout.test.ts:68-82 answers an energy attack with an energy stop and lockout.test.ts:94 uses an 'any' card. Data check confirms Nappa's Energy Aura parses to [{stopAttack, energy, thisCombat, all},{removeFromGameAfterUse}].

findings.title: Attack cards and defense cards are never discarded and never leave the player's hand
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:364 battle-sequence step 16 "The card used to perform the attack is now discarded unless the attack says otherwise." CRD:380 "If you use a card from your hand to attack, you play it on the table from your hand, use the effects of the attack, and then discard it.
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:225-227 - `function discardAttackCards(state, atk, defenseCardUid?): void { }` has an empty body (the comment says "Provisional: log only"); called at combat.ts:272 and combat.ts:281. packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:136-145 only calls findInstance to read the card's ability and never splices it out of hand.
findings.defect: Battle-sequence step 16 is a no-op. No code path in combat.ts or reducer.ts moves the attack card or the defense card from hand to discard.
findings.consequence: Verified at runtime: after a full attack-and-defend exchange the attacker's hand stayed at 2 cards with 0 in discard, and the defender's hand stayed at 5 with 0 in discard. One attack card can therefore be replayed in every Attack Phase for the entire game, and one defense card blocks every attack forever. It also breaks everything downstream of the discard pile: nothing accumulates for the Rejuvenation Step, and hand size never shrinks during combat.

findings.title: Power-stage damage in excess of the target's remaining stages is silently dropped instead of converting to life cards
findings.crdEvidence: CRD L422 "Power stages of damage are dealt by lowering your opponent's power stage ... What happens when that personality runs out of power stages? The remaining power stages are converted to life cards of damage." CRD L436 "When a personality is at 0 and is dealt power stages of damage, those power stages of damage are converted into life cards of damage, and is considered both types of damage." CRD L579 "Any power stages of damage converted into life cards of damage are still discarded from your Life Deck." CRD L157 lists it as a Survival Victory route: "Your opponent discards one card from his Life Deck for each power stage of damage taken by a Personality when that Personality is at their lowest power stage." CRD L821 confirms the conversion happens as damage is dealt. CRD L358 (step 14) "If the attack does 5 or more life cards of damage, the attacker may capture an opponent's Dragon Ball." CRD L1125 Endurance is used "while you are taking damage from an unstopped attack.
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:75-82 (loseStages, `p.stageIndex = Math.max(0, p.stageIndex - n)` at combat.ts:77), called from applyPowerStageDamage at combat.ts:242, which reports `{ type: 'attackResolved', successful: true, powerStages: dmg, lifeCards: 0 }` at combat.ts:243; the dead helper takeLifeCards sits at combat.ts:89; the life-card/Endurance/capture paths are only reachable from combat.ts:285-292 -> 314-337 -> 373-385
findings.defect: loseStages clamps the scouter at index 0 and throws away the surplus; it returns void so no caller could recover it. There is no conversion path anywhere in the engine (grep for convert/overflow in packages/engine/src returns nothing), and the resolution event hard-codes lifeCards: 0 for every physical attack. The helper written for the conversion, takeLifeCards (combat.ts:89), has no call sites in the repo. Every personality in the catalog has zeroStageIndex 0, so array index 0 really is the CRD's "0 power stage" and the clamp is exactly the CRD's overflow point.
findings.consequence: Verified at runtime against packages/engine/dist: a physical attack with base damage 6 against a personality sitting at stage 2 moved it to stage 0 and discarded ZERO life cards (life deck 27 -> 27, discard 0); the CRD requires 4 life cards. The consequences compound across five subsystems: a personality parked at 0 power stages is permanently immune to physical damage; the Survival-Victory route at CRD L157 can never remove a card, so a beaten-down opponent can never be decked by physical attacks and stalling at 0 stages becomes strictly correct play; because capture is gated on life cards actually discarded (combat.ts:374), a physical attack can never reach the 5-life-card Dragon Ball capture threshold; and the defender is never offered Endurance against an ordinary physical attack, so the entire 144-card Endurance pool only ever triggers against energy attacks and the handful of physicals printing a fixed life-card number.

You cannot use your MP's power when an Ally is in control of Combat and vice-versa." CRD:290 lists "5. Use a Personality power" as one of the seven things an Attack Phase can be spent on; CRD:307 lists it as a legal defense; CRD:374 covers attacks made from a Personality Power.

findings.title: The Discard Step never enforces the 1-card hand limit, for either player
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:240-241 - "6) Discard Step: If you are the Attacker and you have more than 1 card in your hand during this step, place all but 1 of your cards into the discard pile. ... you may have no more than 1 card in your hand at the end of this step. Your opponent does the same, right after you discard.
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:79-85; packages/engine/src/turn.ts:36-56
findings.defect: Neither the reducer's `advanceStep` case nor `advanceStep()` itself does anything when the step is or becomes `'discard'` - the step is a pure pass-through. There is no hand-size check anywhere in the engine or server: the only `hand.length` references in engine/server source are abilities.ts:157 (a card-effect discard) and a server test. Nothing trims either player's hand at end of turn.
findings.consequence: Both players accumulate cards without limit across turns. Hand size is the game's central resource constraint - every attack, defense, Drill and Non-Combat is paid for out of a hand that is supposed to be emptied to 1 card every single turn. Without it a player can bank a dozen cards and dump an unanswerable chain of attacks in one Combat Step, and the discard pile never fills, which in turn starves every discard-pile-based card effect.
findings.verifiedBy: CRD:241 reads "...you may have no more than 1 card in your hand at the end of this step.  Your opponent does the same, right after you discard." Neither reducer.ts:79-85 nor turn.ts:36-56 touches the hand on `'discard'`. I grepped `hand.length|zones.hand` across engine+server non-test source: abilities.ts:157 (card-effect discard), noncombat.ts:48/51/57 (playing a card from hand), turn.ts:63 (draw), server/src/redact.ts:28 (view redaction) - that is all. A grep for `hand limit|handLimit|MAX_HAND|all but 1|all but one` across every package returns zero hits. Executed the engine: hands were [3, 0] at the discard step and [4, 0] after passing through discard and rejuvenation into the next turn - no trim. Cannot refute.

findings.title: The Draw Step draws 1 card instead of 3
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:214-215 - "1) Draw Step / If you are the Attacker, draw 3 cards from the top of your Life Deck and put them in your hand.
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/reducer.ts:81
findings.defect: The `advanceStep` case hardcodes a one-card draw: `if (state.step === 'draw') draw(state, state.activePlayerIdx, 1);`. The constant is 1, not 3. Nothing else in the codebase supplements it - `draw()` is called from only four places (reducer.ts:81, reducer.ts:87 for the manual `drawCards` action, combat.ts:64 with `PREPARE_DRAW = 3` for the defender's Prepare Phase, and abilities.ts:205 for card effects). Verified by running the built engine: on turn 2 the new attacker's hand went from 3 to 4, i.e. +1.
findings.consequence: The attacker draws one third of their legal hand every turn while the defender still draws a full 3 in the Prepare Phase. Card flow collapses, the attacker is starved of attacks and defenses, and Life Decks deplete at roughly a third of the correct rate - which directly distorts the Survival Victory clock, the way most real games end, and suppresses the anger and Dragon Ball routes that depend on drawing cards.

findings.title: Drills in play never produce any game effect
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:636 "Drills are constantly in use for their game effects as long as they are in play, and may even create effects multiple times within a turn. You must use a Drill's ability even if you don't want to
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/noncombat.ts:74-75 (`const drill = isDrill(...); const ability = drill ? undefined : ...find(a => a.trigger === 'onPlay')`); packages/shared/src/abilities.ts:14 (`'constant'` trigger declared)
findings.defect: playCard deliberately suppresses a Drill's parsed ability on entry, and nothing anywhere replaces it with continuous application. `trigger === 'constant'` is declared in the Ability union but is read by no engine code, and the enriched catalog contains 0 abilities with that trigger (census of data/cards.tts.enriched.json: onPlay 118, defense 329, attack 751, constant 0). The only reads of `zones.inPlay` in the whole engine are the Mastery test at damage.ts:137, the discard at drills.ts:43-45, playCard's own push/splice at noncombat.ts:58/84-86, and setup.ts:85 - none of them evaluate a Drill. Of the 263 Drill cards in the catalog, 28 carry an onPlay ability that is now dropped and 0 gain anything back.
findings.consequence: Every Drill is inert cardboard. Blue Holding Drill does not cap the opponent's Non-Combat plays, Chiaotzu's Drill does not reduce physical damage, Orange Energy Phasing Drill never applies - a player pays a card and a Non-Combat play for literally nothing, and Drill-based decks cannot function.

You must use a Drill's ability even if you don't want to". packages/engine/src/noncombat.ts:74-75 is exactly as cited: `const drill = isDrill(card.cardId, db); const ability = drill ? undefined : db.get(card.cardId)?.rules?.abilities?.find((a) => a.trigger === 'onPlay');` - the ability is suppressed. I looked for the replacement and found none: grep for `constant` across packages/engine/src returns only packages/shared/src/abilities.ts:14 (`| 'constant'; // Drills / continuous`) and two lines in onplay.test.ts; no engine code branches on it. Every read of `zones.inPlay` in non-test engine code is damage.ts:137 (Mastery), drills.ts:43/45 (discard), noncombat.ts:58/84/86, setup.ts:85, and combat.ts:473 (a uid lookup for stopAttack) - none evaluates a Drill's ability. The one test that touches this, packages/engine/src/onplay.test.ts:189, asserts the opposite of the rule (`assert.equal(s.players[0]!.mp.anger, 2, 'its constant effect did not fire on play')`), so it locks the gap in rather than covering it.

findings.title: A defense card's non-stop secondary effects are silently discarded - only its stopAttack effects are read
findings.crdEvidence: CRD.txt:334 - battle sequence step 6: "Resolve all secondary effects from the defender's card or personality power." CRD L2029 prints Piccolo's Physical Defense as "Stops a physical attack. Gain 4 power stages."; CRD L1633 prints Gohan's Energy Defense as "Stops an energy attack. Raise your anger 1 level.
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/combat.ts:265-277 and combat.ts:471-481 (defenseStops)
findings.defect: When the defender plays a card, `resolveDefense` sets `atk.stopped = true`, then calls `defenseStops(state, opts.cardUid, db)` - which at line 477 does `abilities.flatMap((a) => a.effects).filter((e) => e.kind === 'stopAttack')` - and uses those only to register combat-long lockouts. It then discards the card and moves to the next phase. No other effect on the defense card is ever executed; there is no call to applyOnPlay or any equivalent on the defense path, and `applyIfSuccessful` (abilities.ts:225-243) does not handle `changeAnger` either. 102 parsed abilities with `trigger:'defense'` in data/cards.tts.enriched.json carry a `changeAnger` effect.
findings.consequence: Defence cards deliver only their stop. Gohan's Energy Defense ("Stops an energy attack. Raise your anger 1 level.") stops the attack but grants no anger; Red Forearm Block's "Raise your anger 1 level. Lower your opponent's anger 1 level." does neither; Piccolo's Physical Defense never grants its +4 power stages. Anger raises, power-stage gains, draws and rejuvenation printed on defences are all silently lost. Defending is a primary way anger is gained and lost in this game and none of it happens, so anger accumulates far more slowly than the CRD dictates and anger-denial defense cards are inert. removeFromGameAfterUse is ignored by the same filter, and because discardAttackCards (combat.ts:225-227) is an empty stub the card is never even removed from hand, so the same defence can be replayed against every attack for the whole game.
findings.verifiedBy: CRD.txt:334 reads "6) Resolve all secondary effects from the defender's card or personality power." combat.ts:265-277 is the whole defense-card path: it sets `atk.stopped = true`, loops `for (const e of defenseStops(state, opts.cardUid, db))` only to `addLockout`, then discards and calls `nextAttackPhase`. defenseStops (combat.ts:471-481) throws the rest away at line 477: `return abilities.flatMap((a) => a.effects).filter((e) => e.kind === 'stopAttack');`. There is no applyOnPlay/applyIfSuccessful call anywhere on that path, and applyIfSuccessful (abilities.ts:225-243) handles only stopAttack, stunSkipNextPhase, rejuvenate, movePowerStage and discardCards - no changeAnger. I drove it through the real reducer with a card parsed exactly as the shipped Gohan's Energy Defense (`stopAttack` + `changeAnger user +1`): declareAttack then defend gave `defender anger before: 0 -> after: 0`, log only `P1 stops the attack.` The catalog counts check out - 102 abilities with trigger 'defense' carry a changeAnger effect, and Gohan's Energy Defense and Red Forearm Block parse exactly as described. No test in packages/engine/src/*.test.ts exercises defense-card secondary effects. || Corroborated by the endurance-and-stops audit with a second worked example: Piccolo's Physical Defense parses to [{stopAttack, physical, thisAttack},{changePowerStages, user, +4}] and the +4 never happens, and Nappa's Energy Aura's {removeFromGameAfterUse} is filtered away by the same line 477; combat.ts:225-227 is confirmed an empty stub, so the card stays in hand.

findings.title: The active player can end the Combat Step unilaterally with `advanceStep`, and combat state leaks into later steps
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:279 - "The Attacker gets the first Attack Phase. After his Attack Phase is over, the Defender gets his own Attack Phase. ... This continues until both the Attacker and Defender choose to pass in back-to-back Attack Phases. When that happens - the Combat Step ends.
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/turn.ts:36-56 (with packages/engine/src/combat.ts:161-165 and packages/server/src/room.ts:281)
findings.defect: `advanceStep` has no guard on `state.combat`: from `step === 'combat'` it computes `next = 'discard'` and sets it. Because `delete state.combat` only runs on the wrap into `'draw'` (turn.ts:39-45), `state.combat` survives into the Discard and Rejuvenation Steps. The proper exit, `endCombatStep` (combat.ts:110-114), deletes `combat` first - `advanceStep` does not. The server permits this: `authorize` only checks `state.activePlayerIdx !== seatIdx` for `advanceStep` (room.ts:281), and the client's Advance-step button is enabled whenever it is your turn and no prompt is pending (Board.tsx:188). Separately, `declareAttack` guards on `state.combat` and `phasePlayerIdx` (combat.ts:161-165) but never on `state.step`.
findings.consequence: The attacker attacks once, then presses Advance step and the Combat Step ends - the defender never gets the Attack Phase the rules guarantee them, and gets no chance to pass consecutively. The stale `combat` object then lets attacks continue to be declared and resolved during the Discard and Rejuvenation Steps, and `combat` is finally torn out from under any attack still in progress when the turn wraps.

findings.title: Non-Combat cards resolve and are discarded in the Non-Combat Step instead of being used in the Combat Step
findings.crdEvidence: CRD:629 "They are played in front of you during your Non-Combat Step, and they remain face up on the table until they are used"; CRD:632 "Generally, you use a this card in your Attack Phase in the Combat Step, then you discard them from play"; CRD:288 "Use a Non-Combat card for its effects and then discard it after use" (an Attack Phase option); CRD:305 "Use one of your Non-Combat cards in play if that card has a starburst on it" (a defender option)
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/noncombat.ts:76-93 (resolves the onPlay ability immediately, then splices the card out of inPlay into discard/removed at lines 83-92)
findings.defect: The card's effect fires the instant it is placed, two steps before Combat, and a type 'Non-Combat' card is then moved out of play in the same call. Nothing in combat.ts can use a card sitting in inPlay: declareAttack (combat.ts:152-215) looks up `firstAttackAbility` (trigger 'attack'), resolveDefense (combat.ts:252-310) never calls applyOnPlay, and `applyOnPlay` is invoked from exactly one place - noncombat.ts:78. So the Attack-Phase and starburst-defense use windows do not exist, and CRD:766's requirement that a "____ only" Non-Combat be used while a matching personality is in control of Combat can never be evaluated.
findings.consequence: Timing-sensitive Non-Combat cards are worth less or more than printed. The 33 catalog effects of the form movePowerStage{user,'highest'} fire before the Power-Up Step, so the MP is already at the top of its ladder when powerUp() runs (turn.ts:88 clamps at `ratings.length - 1`) and the entire PUR gain is thrown away; used correctly in the Attack Phase the same card would restore stages spent on energy attacks and damage taken. Conversely, an opponent's "remove a Non-Combat card in play" effect has nothing to target, because the card is already in the discard pile before Combat begins.

STEPS (state.ts:6-14) orders nonCombat before powerUp, and turn.ts:88 is indeed `p.stageIndex = Math.max(0, Math.min(p.stageIndex + delta, ratings.length - 1));`, so a raise-to-highest that fires at play time is erased by the clamp before powerUp adds PUR. applyOnPlay is called from exactly one site (grep: abilities.ts:174 definition, noncombat.ts:78 call). findings.title: A pending deferred Dragon Ball claim suppresses the opponent's immediate Dragon Ball win
findings.crdEvidence: CRD L164/L666: "If you get the last of the 7 Dragon Balls by playing it, you win" - the defer applies only to the player who captured a 7th ball (CRD L167).
findings.engineLocation: packages/engine/src/victory.ts:114
findings.defect: The immediate Dragon Ball branch is guarded by `state.pendingDragonVictory === undefined`, a single global flag rather than a per-player one. While player 0's captured-7th claim is waiting to mature, the guard is false for *every* player in the loop, so player 1 completing their own set is not detected.
findings.consequence: Player 0 captures a 7th ball and their win defers to their next Draw Step. On the intervening turn player 1 plays the last ball of their own set from hand - a win the CRD grants immediately - but nothing happens, and player 0's deferred claim then matures first and takes the game.
findings.verifiedBy: victory.ts:114 is `if (balls && balls.count >= DRAGON_BALL_SET_SIZE && state.pendingDragonVictory === undefined) {`, sitting inside `for (const player of state.players)` (victory.ts:105) - the guard reads a single global field, not `state.pendingDragonVictory !== player.idx`, so it is false for every player in the loop while any claim is pending. The maturation block above it (victory.ts:91-103) only clears the flag when `state.activePlayerIdx === state.pendingDragonVictory && state.step === 'draw'`, so the suppression persists across the whole intervening turn; when it does clear, player 0's endGame at victory.ts:101 returns first. CRD L666 grants the play-it win with no deferral and L167 restricts the deferral to the capturer. The fix is a one-token change to a per-player comparison, so the claim is actionable. victory.test.ts:151-180 covers only the single-player defer, never a second player completing a set during the window.
